Two of our younger members, from Sutton County School, have scored successes. Ken Cuff won the School C.C. Race, and Clifford Hopes the Under 15 Surrey Schools 440 Yards Championship.
Derrick Burfitt, John Brown and Ken Cuff kept together until about half-way, when Burfitt gradually went away to win a good race from John Brown.

The field of 65 was drawn mainly from Youth Clubs and pre-Service Units. Ken Cuff led from the start and beat the local favourite, H. Rouse (whose father is one of our walkers), by four seconds in 20mins. 22secs.
Ken Cuff is another lost to us for the time being. He is now in the Army and stationed near Aldershot, so we may have the pleasure of his company occasionally.

George Murray visited the Hall after five years absence to have a run with the boys before going over the water. Ken Cuff was able to pay us a few visits when stationed near London. He is now up in Scotland with the Black Watch.

Ken Cuff appeared at the Hall recently wearing a kilt, and seemed even bigger than he did on his last visit. Albert Sampson was a competitor at the Club Handicap meeting after three or more years abroad.
Ken Cuff sends a news cutting from Palestine. The news writer says of the "Bels.": "It is their boisterous attitude that is mainly responsible for making them the power they are in the sport to-day."
The final of the 100 yards was a good race and Clements just beat Kemp with Mitchell third. The 880 yards saw Ken Cuff beat A.

Owing to the Surrey Relays on the same day we were short of sprinters for this meeting. Our 4 x 110 team consisted of Underwood, Holtum, Bartlett and Mullen, while our 4 x 440 team was Kennedy, Alan Bishop, Ken.

Archie Bedford finished third in the individual race with Vern Blowfield in fifth place, and then came Jimmy Wood 13th with Len Bishop 16th, and the latter just beat Tom Richards, the well known marathon runner. Others to finish were—Ken Cuff, 36th; J.

Hudson ran well to take first place in the handicap with Ken Cuff second and Mick Tween third. We held a team race with our old friends, Cadogan A.C., in conjunction with the championship, and came out winners with 38 pts. against Cadogan's 157, scoring 8 aside.
Doug Briggs also ran well to finish in 5th place, with Alan Bishop 9th, Ken Cuff 11th, Eric Bishop 12th, Jack Lacey 13th and Mick Tween 14th.
Hudson 66th, Reg Bolam 74th, Ken Stimpson 75th, Alan Bishop 96th, Doug Briggs 100th, Eric Bishop 110th, Ken Cuff 120th, and A.

After having enjoyed the finest winter accommodation and some of the best country that any club in the land can offer, if I ever hear anyone bemoaning their lot at Belgrave Hall again I'll recommend them to a couple of helpimgs of the South East Essex League, and all that it implies. I'm sure Ken Cuff will back me up.
